title: The intersection of coefficient subrings is the pth-power image
statement: Let p be prime, k a field of characteristic p, and (t_i) indexed by I a p-basis of k over k^p. Let n,m be nonnegative integers and A = k[[x_1,...,x_n]][y_1,...,y_m]. For each finite J in I, let kJ be the subfield generated by k^p and the t_i outside J, and AJ the subring defined exactly by coefficients in kJ and nonzero coefficients only at p-divisible x and y exponents. For every f in A, f belongs to every AJ if and only if f = h^p for some h in A. The power-series and polynomial rings are [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] and [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], and p-basis means the bounded monomials form a basis as in [def-weil-pbc-free-module].

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07P5 (lemma-power-series-ring-subfields, line 11521) and its proof; properties (2)-(4) are conditions (1)-(3) of Lemma Tag 07P4 (lemma-intersection-subfields), written out; tags verified in stacks-project/tags/tags

proof.text: Let P be the intermediate field generated by all pth powers. For each finite J, let M(J) be the P-span of the bounded p-basis monomials whose exponents on J are zero. Reduce arbitrary monomial exponents modulo p to prove membership in this span; the removed powers of t_i are scalars in P. Span induction in both factors proves closure under multiplication. The span contains 1, and for x nonzero it contains x^(-1)=(x^p)^(-1)*x^(p-1), since x^p belongs to P. Subfield closure induction therefore shows kJ is contained in M(J). For c in every kJ, take J to be the finite union of supports of the basis indices occurring in b.repr c. The basis support characterization of a span forces every such index to vanish on J, hence to be zero. Thus c is a scalar times the constant basis vector 1 and belongs to P. Finally P is contained in the field range of Frobenius: all its pth-power generators are in that range, and Frobenius fixes the image of ZMod p because its elements are natural-number casts. Membership in the field range gives a pth root of c. This is implemented by the proved private helper pBasisCoefficientIntersection; no finite-dimensional inverse argument is used.

If f belongs to every AJ, use hAJ for each J and the coefficient-field argument to obtain a pth root for every coefficient; use J empty to obtain p-divisibility of every exponent with a nonzero coefficient. For a power series c, construct a root h by setting h(a) to the chosen root of coeff(p*a,c). The coefficientwise Frobenius identity proves h^p=c: at p-divisible indices use coeff_expand_smul, and at the other indices use coeff_expand_of_not_dvd and the given vanishing. Each nonzero polynomial coefficient c_g has some nonzero power-series coefficient, forcing g to be p-divisible. Its monomial consequently has a root, by monomial_pow and the power-series root construction. A finite sum of roots of all monomials of f gives a polynomial root, using sum_pow_char and f.as_sum. Conversely map_frobenius_expand for polynomials followed by the same formula for power series shows each coefficient of h^p is a pth power and each nonzero index is p-divisible. The pth-power coefficient belongs to kJ by subset_closure, and hAJ gives h^p in AJ for every J. All helpers are proved and remain private.

lean.statement:
theorem powerSeriesSubringIntersection
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime]
    (k : Type u) [Field k] [CharP k p]
    (I : Type w) (t : I → k)
    (hpb : ∃ b : Module.Basis
      {E : I →₀ ℕ // ∀ i : I, E i < p}
      (IntermediateField.adjoin (ZMod p) (Set.range (fun x : k => x ^ p))) k,
      ∀ E, b E = (E : I →₀ ℕ).prod (fun i e => t i ^ e))
    (n m : ℕ) (kJ : Finset I → Subfield k)
    (hkJ : ∀ J, kJ J = Subfield.closure
      (Set.range (fun x : k => x ^ p) ∪ {x : k | ∃ i : I, i ∉ J ∧ t i = x}))
    (AJ : Finset I → Subring (MvPolynomial (Fin m) (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) k)))
    (hAJ : ∀ J f, f ∈ AJ J ↔
      ∀ (a : Fin n →₀ ℕ) (g : Fin m →₀ ℕ),
        MvPowerSeries.coeff a (MvPolynomial.coeff g f) ∈ kJ J ∧
        (MvPowerSeries.coeff a (MvPolynomial.coeff g f) ≠ 0 →
          (∀ i, p ∣ a i) ∧ (∀ j, p ∣ g j))) :
    ∀ f : MvPolynomial (Fin m) (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) k),
      (∀ J, f ∈ AJ J) ↔ ∃ h, h ^ p = f
